headline: Hurricane Nolo, nearing Category 5 strength, tracks away from Hawaii's main islands

source_records.source_name: U.S. National Hurricane Center / Central Pacific Hurricane Center (NOAA)

Hurricane Nolo had maximum sustained winds of 145 mph as a Category 4 storm, with its eye located several hundred miles south-southwest of Honolulu.

caption:
🇺🇸 Hurricane Nolo, a major Category 4 storm with 145 mph winds and briefly flirting with Category 5 strength, is tracking well south and southwest of Hawaii's main islands after an earlier scare, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said Sept. 28, 2026. The storm's most dangerous winds are instead aimed at the uninhabited Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument, sparing the populated islands a direct hit, though high surf and heavy rain continue there.

🇪🇸 El huracan Nolo, una tormenta mayor de categoria 4 con vientos de 145 mph que llego a rozar la categoria 5, se desplaza bien al sur y suroeste de las islas principales de Hawai tras un susto inicial, informo el Centro Nacional de Huracanes de EE.UU. el 28 de septiembre de 2026. Los vientos mas peligrosos de la tormenta se dirigen en cambio hacia el deshabitado Monumento Nacional Marino Papahanaumokuakea, librando a las islas pobladas de un impacto directo, aunque persisten el oleaje fuerte y las lluvias intensas.

Sources: NOAA National Hurricane Center / UPI / Weather.com — Sept. 28, 2026.
